stem: A 30-year-old woman is 30 weeks pregnant. She is RhD-negative and previously delivered an RhD-positive baby abroad, after which she did not receive anti-D immunoglobulin. Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist and can cause acute dystonic reactions, particularly in young people. Oculogyric crisis, torticollis, jaw spasm and tongue protrusion are typical. Serotonin syndrome usually includes serotonergic drug exposure, agitation, hyperreflexia, clonus and autonomic instability. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome develops over longer periods with severe rigidity, fever and raised creatine kinase. A generalised seizure would involve impaired consciousness and rhythmic convulsions. Tetanus is not temporally linked to metoclopramide and would not present so rapidly after the drug.

Clinical context: Drug-induced movement disorders are common iatrogenic presentations in acute care and are usually treated with an anticholinergic such as procyclidine.

Correct answer: A - Quantitative rapid plasma reagin titre

Treponemal tests such as EIA and TPPA often remain positive for life after treated syphilis, so they cannot reliably distinguish old treated infection from reinfection. A quantitative non-treponemal test such as RPR provides a titre that supports assessment of active disease and is used to monitor treatment response. Repeating TPPA adds little. Clinical context: Sexual health clinics use both treponemal and non-treponemal tests, with RPR or VDRL titres guiding follow-up after treatment.

Correct answer: A - Treat the sepsis and give appropriate blood product support for bleeding, including cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen replacement

This patient has sepsis-associated DIC with active bleeding, thrombocytopenia, prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen and high D-dimer. Management is treatment of the underlying sepsis plus supportive transfusion guided by bleeding and results, including platelets, FFP and cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen replacement when fibrinogen is low. Heparin may be considered in selected predominantly thrombotic DIC but is not the sole treatment for active bleeding. Vitamin K alone does not address consumption coagulopathy. Aspirin would worsen bleeding. Waiting until platelets are below 10 is inappropriate in active bleeding.

Clinical context: DIC is usually secondary to a major trigger such as sepsis, trauma, malignancy or obstetric catastrophe.

Guideline anchor: British Society for Haematology guidance on DIC principles

Exam tip: In DIC, always treat the underlying cause; give blood products when there is bleeding or a high-risk procedure.

Correct answer: A - Asbestosis

Pipe lagging is a classic asbestos exposure. Pleural plaques strongly indicate prior asbestos exposure, and lower-zone reticular shadowing with bibasal crackles supports asbestosis. Coal workers' pneumoconiosis and silicosis more typically cause upper-zone nodular disease related to coal dust or silica exposure. Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is linked to organic antigen exposure and often has episodic symptoms. Sarcoidosis more commonly causes bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and upper-zone involvement.

Clinical context: Asbestos-related disease may present decades after exposure and includes pleural plaques, asbestosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma.

Guideline anchor: standard UK respiratory and occupational medicine practice

Exam tip: Pleural plaques plus basal fibrosis in a former asbestos worker points to asbestosis.
